notes.Day 3: Your 30-day field experiment starts after this touchpoint and continues after the ten teaching touchpoints. Use four recording windows: Days 1–7, 8–14, 15–21, and 22–30. Record the first eligible moment in each window, or a no-opportunity result. The final window includes Days 29 and 30.
notes.Day 7: The story below looks ahead to the end of a month. Your own experiment is still running. Use this touchpoint to practise how you will close it honestly after Day 30.
notes.Day 8: Interim review: use only the evidence you have recorded so far. Keep the number of recorded weeks separate from the 30-day experiment length. Do not count future weeks, missing records, or no-opportunity periods as completed practice.
notes.Day 9: Explore where else you could apply the method while your first experiment continues. A transfer plan is not evidence that transfer has happened.
notes.Day 10: After these ten touchpoints, keep your tracker available and continue recording until the end of Day 30. Finish all four recording windows, including Days 29–30 in the final window. After Day 30, return to the Evidence Review method from Day 8 using the complete record. Compare your prediction with what happened, note any missing or no-opportunity periods, and update your Launch Investigation Profile. The ten-touchpoint reflection is an interim reflection; it does not confirm experiment completion.
notes.Certificate: Certificate template for the final follow-up: complete this only after all 30 calendar days and the final evidence review. Finishing the ten teaching touchpoints alone does not award this certificate.
